name: TEMPI Syndrome
aliases: Telangiectasias, Elevated erythropoietin, Monoclonal gammopathy, Perinephric fluid collections, Intrapulmonary shunting syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed diagnostic criteria for TEMPI syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of monoclonal gammopathy (usually IgG or IgA)
Perinephric fluid collections detected by imaging
Evidence of intrapulmonary shunting causing hypoxemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of monoclonal gammopathy, elevated erythropoietin, and telangiectasias; supportive findings include perinephric fluid collections and intrapulmonary shunting
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by laboratory and imaging findings; response to plasma cell-directed therapy supports diagnosis

laboratory: Monoclonal gammopathy detected by serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation
Secondary erythrocytosis with increased hemoglobin and hematocrit
imaging: Perinephric fluid collections on ultrasound or CT scan
Evidence of intrapulmonary shunting on contrast echocardiography or nuclear medicine scans
genetic: No known genetic mutations identified; etiology is idiopathic or related to plasma cell dyscrasia
other: Improvement with plasma cell-directed therapies (e.g., bortezomib, lenalidomide)
Hypoxemia responsive to treatment of underlying plasma cell disorder

distinguishingFeatures: Primary bone marrow disorder with JAK2 mutation
Absence of telangiectasias and perinephric fluid collections
Genetic disorder with recurrent epistaxis and mucocutaneous telangiectasias
No monoclonal gammopathy or elevated erythropoietin
Arteriovenous malformations rather than perinephric fluid collections

redFlags: Presence of perinephric fluid collections on imaging
references: Sykes DB, et al. TEMPI syndrome: a novel multisystem disease characterized by telangiectasias, erythrocytosis, monoclonal gammopathy, perinephric fluid collections, and intrapulmonary shunting. Blood. 2011.
Sykes DB, et al. Clinical and laboratory features of TEMPI syndrome: a case series and review. Haematologica. 2017.
Orphanet: TEMPI syndrome. Orphanet Report Series, 2023.
